title: common/libnetwork: skip internal networks for pesto forwarding ip
body:
When ports are published they should not be used for internal networks as they do not allow external connections normally. This is how it always worked as root but with rootlessport internal networks could still use published ports as the traffic was proxied directly into the netns.

With the new pasta forwarding this no longer works as the return route is not there. That leads to only a connection working one way which is the worst of all options.
So because we do not want published ports on internal networks skip them here. This ensures when one internal and one public network is connected at the same time the ports are published on the external network.

comments.body:
> I think it would be good to have the e2e test as an optional follow-up in Podman.

I have a system test written locally, but the test passes with and without this change as right now only the return route is broken so in terms of tcp we need a full round trip. I guess I could try some udp connection instead to show traffic passes one way currently but setting up udp listeners and making sure they are ready and so on is always extra complexity compared to a proper tcp handshake.

Anyhow we have no actual --internal runtime test in podman AFAICS so I guess this test still makes sense. 
```
# https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29792
# CANNOT BE PARALLELIZED: switches rootless_port_forwarder, unsafe with other containers running
@test "internal networks ports publish" {
    # For rootless we only want to test pasta forwarding, rootlessport support publish with internal.
    local conffile=$PODMAN_TMPDIR/pasta-forwarder.conf
    cat >$conffile <<EOF
[network]
rootless_port_forwarder="pasta"
EOF
    export CONTAINERS_CONF_OVERRIDE=$conffile

    local net1="net1-internal-$(safename)"
    local net2="net2-$(safename)"
    run_podman network create --internal $net1
    run_podman network create $net2

    HOST_PORT=$(random_free_port)
    URL=http://127.0.0.1:$HOST_PORT/index.txt

    local cname="c-$(safename)"

    # Create a test file with random content
    INDEX=$PODMAN_TMPDIR/hello.txt
    local random="$(random_string)"
    echo "$random" > $INDEX

    # Bind-mount this file with a different name to a container running httpd
    run_podman run -d --name $cname -p "$HOST_PORT:80" \
            --network $net1 \
            -v $INDEX:/var/www/index.txt:Z \
            -w /var/www \
            $IMAGE /bin/busybox-extras httpd -f -p 80

    # curl should fail
    run curl --max-time 1 -s -S $URL
    echo "$output"
    assert "$status" =~ '7|28' "curl should fail for internal only network"

    run_podman network connect $net2 $cname

    run curl --max-time 3 -s -S $URL
    echo "$output"
    assert "$status" -eq 0 "curl should work once connected to regular network"
    assert "$output" == "$random"

    run_podman rm -f -t0 $cname
    run_podman network rm $net1 $net2
}
```
